channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: AKASA launches autonomous AI for inpatient coding — the mid-cycle "holy grail" touching 1 in 10 US hospital discharges
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AKASA launched an autonomous AI platform for inpatient medical coding and clinical documentation today — the 'holy grail' of the hospital revenue cycle, with customers representing one in ten US inpatient discharges.

item.title: October is "Holistic AI Governance Month": 31 days of layered controls after a summer of rogue AI agents
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AIGE Global Advisors declared October 2026 'Holistic AI Governance Month' today — 31 days, one idea a day, across six layers of AI agent control. It follows a summer of rogue agent incidents, and a certification program opens in November.

item.title: GIGABYTE adds a 64GB AI TOP ATOM to its DGX Spark desktop lineup — desktop AI gets a smaller entry point
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: GIGABYTE announced a 64GB version of its AI TOP ATOM desktop AI box today, adding a lower tier to its NVIDIA DGX Spark-based lineup. It ships October 23 — and up to four units can be clustered into a 256GB memory pool.

item.title: Amazon wants to sell $8B of Nvidia chips to investors — then rent them back
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Amazon is reportedly in talks to move roughly $8 billion of Nvidia's Grace Blackwell chips into an investor-backed vehicle and lease them back — the latest sign that Wall Street, not just Big Tech balance sheets, is financing the AI buildout.

item.title: FLUX 3 Image is here: Black Forest Labs ships multi-step editing that leaves the rest of the picture alone
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Black Forest Labs released FLUX 3 Image, the image product of its FLUX 3 family — multi-step, region-precise editing up to 4K, with API access 50% off through October 8 and open weights promised in the coming weeks.

item.title: LG Uplus partners with OptAI to quadruple GPU throughput with token optimization
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: South Korea's LG Uplus said today it is teaming up with AI optimization startup OptAI to develop token optimization technology for server GPUs — targeting 4× the tokens per GPU and lower power draw for large-scale AI services.

item.title: Give your AI agent a browser: hands-on with browser-use, the 117K-star library
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: browser-use (nearly 117K stars, MIT) turns any LLM into an agent that clicks, types, and scrolls like a human. Install the Python library, wire up your model, and drive a real browser from a script — in about 15 minutes.

item.title: Searchable launches Prompt Universe: your AI visibility score may cover 2% of what buyers actually ask
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AI visibility platform Searchable launched Prompt Universe today, mapping the full range of questions buyers ask AI about a brand — often tens or hundreds of thousands — before narrowing down to the set worth tracking.

item.title: Vaultz Capital sells 47 bitcoin to back an unnamed GPU-memory startup at a £90M valuation
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: London-listed Vaultz Capital sold 47 bitcoin from its treasury to invest £3M in a stealth AI infrastructure startup whose software claims to let a single GPU run workloads that would otherwise need a whole cluster. The startup’s name was not disclosed.

item.title: 62% of Canadian workers say AI is eroding their skills, IBM finds — while HR barely uses AI itself
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: IBM's Institute for Business Value published a 10,300-person global study today: 62% of Canadian employees worry AI is eroding their skills — 69% of them say it already has — while 63% of Canadian organizations barely use AI inside HR.

item.title: Publishers ship Content Telemetry v1.0: a five-stage tracker for AI's use of their content — and pitch OpenAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft on a licensing board
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The Guardian, FT, AP, BBC and other publishers released the first version of the SPUR Content Telemetry standard today — a five-stage protocol that makes AI agents report how they retrieve, ground, cite, present and engage with journalism.

item.title: Viral 'AI torture chamber' experiment spotlights the Pain Axis paper — a steering vector, not felt pain
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Reddit exploded this week over an 'AI torture chamber' — a live experiment steering LLMs with a 'pain direction' from a September interpretability paper. The paper is real, the experiment is live, and GitHub never took it down. But 'felt pain' is not what the research found.

item.title: Skills for Real Engineers: hands-on with Matt Pocock's 274K-star agent skills
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Matt Pocock's agent-skills collection just topped GitHub's trending AI repos with 274,000+ stars. Install the engineering skills — /grill-me, /tdd, /code-review — into your coding agent and run a real change through them, start to finish.

item.title: Merge models, don't just train them: hands-on model merging with MergeKit
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: SLERP, task arithmetic, and TIES/DARE, explained by actually running them: merge Qwen2.5-0.5B with its instruct sibling on a CPU, verify the identity merge, and measure what the midpoint really does.

item.title: Write your own GPU kernels in 30 lines of Python: a hands-on guide to TileLang
item.dc:creator: Elena Vasquez
item.description: The fastest models alive run on hand-tuned GPU kernels. TileLang is an 8,167-star Pythonic tile-level language that compiles to CUDA, ROCm, Metal, and Ascend — here’s the 30-line tiled matmul that opens the door.

item.title: arXiv caps every author at two submissions a month as AI-generated spam overwhelms its moderators
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: arXiv now limits every submitter to two papers per calendar month and three active submissions at a time — the preprint server’s bluntest response yet to AI-generated submission spam. September brought a record 40,363 submissions and nearly 9,000 support tickets.

item.title: Stop vibe-coding: give your AI agent a real methodology — hands-on with Superpowers
item.dc:creator: Elena Vasquez
item.description: Your coding agent doesn’t need more tools — it needs a methodology. Superpowers is a 294K-star skills framework that forces your agent to brainstorm, plan, TDD, and review like a senior team. Hands-on: install, bootstrap injection, and a full loop.

item.title: A developer turned any website into a stickman destruction sandbox — built with Claude Opus 5.5 over a weekend
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: u/HugoDzz spent a weekend building a destruction sandbox that turns any website URL into a playable stickman level — with Claude Opus 5.5 as his pair programmer. The r/ClaudeAI thread pulled 2,500 upvotes in a day, and the game had already gone viral on X.

item.title: FBI arrests California tech CEO over alleged $300M AI-chip smuggling pipeline to China
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Federal prosecutors say Earthmade Computer CEO Greg Lui routed export-controlled AI servers through Singapore and Malaysia into China — using false paperwork and staged dummy servers to fool inspectors. He faces up to 50 years.

item.title: Sony brings AI upscaling to the base PS5: QSSR, a slimmed-down PSSR, debuts in Wolverine and Ghost of Yōtei
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Sony announced QSSR on October 1, a new performance tier of its AI upscaling for the base PlayStation 5 — shipping the same day in Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yōtei.

item.title: OpenClaw: run your own self-hosted AI agent on WhatsApp and Telegram — hands-on with the 391K-star personal assistant
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenClaw is the 391K-star open-source personal AI assistant that runs on your own machine and answers inside WhatsApp, Telegram, and 20+ other chat apps. I installed it, connected Telegram, and set up a scheduled briefing — here is every verified step.

item.title: OpenAI fires three safety researchers for allegedly sharing confidential data with an outside AI-safety group
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI parted ways with three researchers on October 1, accusing them of mishandling sensitive information with an external AI-safety organization. The Wall Street Journal named them: Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni.

item.title: PaleBlueDot AI raises $200M at $3.2B to scale 'Super Intelligence' compute — with $5B in contracts already signed
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The Palo Alto neocloud closed a $200 million Series C led by ComputeCore at a $3.2 billion valuation, eight months after a $150 million Series B — and says it has already signed over $5 billion in customer contracts across its GPU clusters, marketplace, and serverless inference.

item.title: MoneyPrinterTurbo: turn any topic into a finished short video — hands-on with the 128K-star AI video pipeline
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Hands-on with the open-source pipeline that scripts, voices, subtitles, and renders vertical short videos end to end — including a zero-API-key run you can do today.

item.title: Satlyt raises $8M to run AI models on other companies' satellites — first flight launches Thursday on a SpaceX rocket
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Ex-Google and SpaceX product manager Rama Afullo raised an $8M seed for Satlyt, the self-described "Android" of orbital compute. Its code flies Thursday on a SpaceX rocket — alongside the first prototype of Google's Project Suncatcher space data center.
